segments.speaker: Mara
segments.body: Welcome back to Harbor Voices, the show about small ports and the people who keep them running.

segments.speaker: Mara
segments.body: Today we are at Grey Point with Tobias Renn, who has kept the lighthouse there for 24 years.

segments.speaker: Tobias
segments.body: Thanks, Mara. The lamp still burns colza oil, about 16 litres a night in the winter months.

segments.speaker: Mara
segments.body: How did the Grey Point Trust decide to keep the old lamp instead of fitting an electric one?

segments.speaker: Tobias
segments.body: The Grey Point Trust voted on it in March, and the old lamp won by 34 votes to nine.

segments.speaker: Tobias
segments.body: An electric lamp would have cost the Trust 110 thousand dollars before a single night of light.

segments.speaker: Mara
segments.body: Tobias Renn keeps a ledger of every ship that passes, and the ledger is the reason we came.

segments.speaker: Tobias
segments.body: The first entry is from 1902, a coal barge called the Wren, and we have 214 volumes now.

segments.speaker: Mara
segments.body: What does the ledger tell you about the harbour that the official port records do not?

segments.speaker: Tobias
segments.body: The port records count tonnage, but the ledger records weather, crews and who was late and why.

segments.speaker: Tobias
segments.body: Last winter the ledger showed 48 ships turning back at the bar, twice the number of the year before.

segments.speaker: Mara
segments.body: The Harbour Board reportedly disputes that count and says its own radar logs show far fewer.

segments.speaker: Tobias
segments.body: It is unclear whose count is right, because the radar at North Quay was down for most of January.

segments.speaker: Mara
segments.body: Why does it matter to a fishing family in the town whether the count is forty or eighty?

segments.speaker: Tobias
segments.body: Because the dredging budget follows the count, and the Harbour Board sets the dredging budget every spring.

segments.speaker: Tobias
segments.body: If the bar is not dredged, the larger boats of the Northwind Cooperative cannot land their catch here.

segments.speaker: Mara
segments.body: The Northwind Cooperative lands about 64 percent of the fish sold at the Saturday market.

segments.speaker: Tobias
segments.body: I think the town forgets how much of its income crosses that bar in the dark every single night.

segments.speaker: Mara
segments.body: Let us talk about the keeper's day, because people imagine it as lonely and quiet work.

segments.speaker: Tobias
segments.body: I trim the wick at dusk, wind the clockwork every four hours, and write the ledger before I sleep.

segments.speaker: Tobias
segments.body: The clockwork was built by Halden and Sons in 1911 and it has stopped only three times since then.

segments.speaker: Mara
segments.body: Could a young person still learn this trade, or does the knowledge end with the keepers we have?

segments.speaker: Tobias
segments.body: Two apprentices started with the Trust this year, and one of them already reads the tide tables better than I do.

segments.speaker: Mara
segments.body: The Grey Point Trust pays for the apprentices out of visitor tickets and a small grant from the county.

segments.speaker: Tobias
segments.body: We had 10600 visitors last summer, which is more than the lighthouse has ever seen in one season.

segments.speaker: Mara
segments.body: Does the crowd change the place, and is there a point where the Trust would turn people away?

segments.speaker: Tobias
segments.body: We cap the tower at twelve people an hour, and nobody climbs after the lamp has been lit.

segments.speaker: Mara
segments.body: There is a plan from the county to build a visitor centre on the meadow behind the keeper's cottage.

segments.speaker: Tobias
segments.body: I am against the visitor centre where it is drawn, because the meadow is where the terns nest in May.

segments.speaker: Mara
segments.body: Supporters of the plan say the visitor centre would bring thirty jobs to a town that badly needs them.

segments.speaker: Tobias
segments.body: Both things are true, and I would rather see the centre built at North Quay beside the old customs shed.

segments.speaker: Mara
segments.body: What would you ask the Harbour Board if you had five minutes in front of all its members?

segments.speaker: Tobias
segments.body: I would ask them to publish the radar logs, so that the town can compare them with the ledger.

segments.speaker: Mara
segments.body: That is a fair request, and we will put the same question to the Harbour Board ourselves next week.

segments.speaker: Tobias
segments.body: Whatever they answer, the lamp will be lit at dusk, as it has been on every night since 1902.

segments.speaker: Mara
segments.body: Tobias Renn, keeper of the Grey Point lighthouse, thank you for showing us the ledger and the lamp.

segments.speaker: Mara
segments.body: Next time on Harbor Voices we visit the ice house at North Quay and the family that still runs it.
